title: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report — US crude, gasoline and distillate stocks (10:30 ET, flash-PMI morning)
source: EST: derived from the publisher's own stated rule plus the publisher's own 2026 exception table, both fetched direct 2026-09-16 (HTTP 200). (1) eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/schedule.php states verbatim: 'The wpsrsummary.pdf, overview.pdf, and Tables 1-14 in CSV and XLS formats, are released to the web site after 10:30 a.m. eastern time on Wednesday.' (2) The same page's Holiday Release Schedule lists every 2026 exception — data for the weeks ending 01-16, 02-13, 05-22, 09-04, 10-09 and 11-06 — and the week ending 2026-09-18 is NOT among them, so the standard Wednesday 10:30 ET rule applies unmodified and lands the release on 2026-09-23. (3) eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/ fetched direct the same day (HTTP 200) still showed the pre-09-16 state ('Data for week ending Sep. 4, 2026 / Release Date: Sep. 10, 2026 / Next Release Date: Sep. 16, 2026'), so the landing page does NOT yet name 09-23 and this date rests on the rule plus the exception table, not on the publisher naming it — a real limit, recorded rather than glossed. Status stays estimate on the same standing schema gap eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16 documented: market-events-data.ts defines no confirmed-source prefix for an EIA release schedule, and adding an EIA: prefix is a schema change, not this lane's call. Checked 2026-09-16
notes: PROPOSED BY THE ADJACENCY SWEEP OF sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23, 2026-09-16 (D-7). WHY THIS GAP MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER: that ledger's leg 6 asserts the 2026-09-23 09:30-10:30 ET window is clean of tracked competitors, and its forward test FT-sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23-1 carries a VOID clause that fires only if a named dated catalyst lands INSIDE 09:30-10:30 ET that morning. The calendar already tracks eia-weekly-petroleum-status-2026-09-16 and -2026-09-30 but skipped the Wednesday between them, which is the flash PMI's own morning — so the nearest untracked US catalyst to a window this calendar calls clean was invisible to it. Proposing it CONFIRMS rather than breaks the clean-window claim: 10:30 ET is the boundary, 45 minutes after the flash window closes, so it does not void the forward test; it makes the nearest competitor a named, dated entry instead of an unexamined blank. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is tiered low deliberately, matching the 09-16 sibling: no house playbook is energy-keyed, no tracked symbol carries direct crude exposure, and symbols is left EMPTY on purpose. The regime is the reason it is worth tracking at all rather than the reason to size it: the 2026-09-11 CPI close-out scored gasoline +3.9% as 'over one third of the monthly all items increase', and Brent is above $100 (~$108.47 on 2026-09-15 per the fomc-2026-09-16 ledger) on a backwardated curve. The 09-16 sibling's own measurement is the caution against reading this print as a price-setter: its prior release (2026-09-10) was bearish on every headline and WTI still closed +6.69%. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Proposer's ledger: docs/research/events/sp-global-flash-us-pmi-2026-09-23.md.
